record.body: Signature whale-song analogues are long, structured, invented songs in the manner of humpback song, organised into phrases and themes and repeated for long periods, but composed as original Signature designs rather than transcribed from any real whale. A Signature song analogue is defined by its theme sequence, its phrase durations, and its pitch range, all stated as design parameters, and the pair explains how a population of Signature singers could share and gradually change a song by copying, as a model of cultural transmission. This is a design exercise, labeled Signature, not a field recording and not a claim about any real whale population. This record covers the Signature biophony layer, distinct from ocean Signature geophony and Signature anthrophony such as designed ship noise.
